title: MIG fragmentation-aware attention tiling + clock coordination optimizer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: On MIG-partitioned hosts we observe suboptimal kernel selection and attention-tiling choices when MIG slices are fragmented or operating with mixed clock states. This leads to elevated p95/p99 tail latency and lower overall throughput for prefill/decode workloads, especially for H100 and L40S fleets with mixed A100->H100 migrations and A10 inference tiers.

Goal: Implement a fragmentation-aware optimizer inside the serving runtime that: (1) computes an affinity score for available MIG slices and active partitions, (2) selects attention tiling + kernel variant combinations that minimize cross-slice memory traffic, and (3) coordinates soft clock steering (preferred clock domains / power profiles) with the scheduler to reduce kernel latency variance. The optimizer must integrate with existing prefill/decode scheduler and not regress single-request latency or correctness.
acceptance_criteria: p95 token latency reduced by >=12% on H100 MIG-fragmented traces compared to baseline
p99 token latency reduced by >=8% across mixed L40S/A10 clusters
No increase >2% in median latency for non-MIG hosts
Unit/integration tests covering kernel selection matrix and tie-break rules
Automated nightly perf job demonstrates stable improvement for 14 days
Feature gated flag and canary rollout with clear rollback thresholds
approach: Phase 1: Telemetry and profiling - augment runtime to log per-request MIG affinity, kernel variant chosen, clock state, and attention tiling heuristic (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Offline analysis - build cost model that estimates execution time for kernel variants under different MIG fragmentation/clock states (1 week)

Phase 3: Optimizer implementation - add a lightweight decision layer in scheduler to score candidate (slice, kernel, tiling, clock-suggestion) tuples. Implement fast-path for common sequence lengths (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Clock coordination - implement soft clock steering API to suggest switching GPU clocks within allowed SLAs, with backoff if thermal or tenant constraints present (1 week)
Phase 5: Integration testing + canary rollout - internal canary -> 5% -> 20% -> full (2 weeks)
Fallback: if optimizer fails or triggers regressions, fall back to existing kernel selection policy and revert clock suggestions
milestones: 2026-03-06: Offline model and matrix uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-perf/mig-matrix/2026-03)
2026-03-17: Scheduler optimizer alpha merged behind runtime flag (PR #5917)
test_plan: Microbenchmarks: run kernel-level microbench across H100/L40S/A10 variants with representative seq-lens (32/128/512) and batch sizes (1/8/32)
System perf: end-to-end prefill+decode traces replay against cluster with synthetic MIG fragmentation patterns
Soak test: 48h run on dedicated MIG fleet to validate thermal/power stability
Regression suite: ensure no token-level correctness changes and compare outputs for 1000 golden prompts
Canary metrics: track per-tenant p50/p95/p99, kernel-switch rate, clock-change rate, CPU/GPU utilization, and thermal events
rollout_plan: Nightly feature toggle off by default
Internal canary: enable for infra team traffic (2-3 hosts) + run perf harness
External canary: enable 5% of hosted traffic for non-enterprise models
Monitor for 48h windows at each step; rollback if p99 increases >5% or error rate increases >0.1%
After stable canary, ramp to 20% then full in weekly increments
risks: Clock steering requests could collide with tenant-imposed clock constraints or maintenance windows
Aggressive tiling choices might increase memory copy overhead on certain kernels (A10 edge cases)
Telemetry volume growth - per-request logs could add significant cardinality if not sampled
Thermal pressure could force GPU downclocking causing oscillation between steering suggestions and automatic throttles
